title: Gizmo Axis Setting
content: ### Objective There are three different Gizmo types in Marvelous Designer. Select and utilize it as needed. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Gizmo 3D Window ▶ Right-click (on the 3D window) ▶ Gizmo ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Gizmo 3D Window ▶ Right-click (on the 3D window) ▶ Gizmo 2\. Select a desired Gizmo. 3\. Select an object with Select/Move Tool. → The chosen type of Gizmo appears. 4\. Click the axis of the Gizmo ▶ Drag it to the desired location. → The chosen object moves along with the Gizmo. Screen Coordinate Gizmo | Screen Coordinate Gizmo is based on the camera axis. Change the camera view in order to change the gizmo axis. Selected object moves along with the camera axis. ---|--- Local Coordinate Gizmo | Local Coordinate Gizmo axis is based on following the native direction of an object. Mainly usable when designing poses from the avatar's X-ray joint points. Selected object moves to native direction of an object. World Coordinate Gizmo | World Coordinate Gizmo is based on 3D space regardless of screens or objects. Selected object moves based on 3D space regardless of screens or objects.
content_description: This webpage aims to guide users in selecting and utilizing the three different Gizmo types in Marvelous Designer for effective object manipulation within the 3D environment.

title: Reset Buttonhole Style Property
content: ### Objective Reset buttonhole item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset → The buttonhole item properties are now being reset back to default value.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to resetting buttonhole item properties to their default values within the Object Browser interface.

title: Zoom Extents All (3D)
content: ### Objective Set the view in the 3D window to reveal all Patterns or center the 3D view to the center of the 3D grid. ### Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Zoom Extents All ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Zoom Extents All → The 3D view is adjusted to reveal all 3D Patterns, or resets the view to the center of the 3D grid.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting the 3D view to display all Patterns or center the view within the 3D grid using the right-click pop-up menu.

title: 3D Garment View Controls
content: Zoom in and change view in the 3D window at once. ### Change Camera View Right click on the 3D window to access the pop-up menu. Select the desired view among Front, 3/4 Left, Back, Left, Right, 3/4 Right, Top, Button, or use respective shortcuts (2, 3, 8, 6, 4, 1, 5, 0) to change camera view instantly. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438530878489) ※ Note: #### Camera Direction Change Standards Using the corresponding menu while the avatar is facing a different direction on the screen changes the camera's angle according to the avatar. #### ### Zoom In/Out Shortcuts Zoom In: Hold down the + key on the keyboard to zoom in the 3D window. Zoom Out: Hold down the - key on the keyboard to zoom out the 3D window. ### Zoom to Selected Zoom in/out and rotate the 3D window using the selected Pattern or item as the focal point. Select the desired Pattern or item in the 3D window and locate Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Zoom Extends All, Or press the shortcut key F to enlarge the selected object at a fixed scale at the middle and control the view according to it. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438531036313)
content_description: Easily navigate and manipulate your 3D view by changing camera angles and zooming in or out with intuitive shortcuts and menu options.

title: Move Avatars & Garments to Default Position
content: ### Objective Move avatars and garments to default position. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) ▶ Move Avatars & Garments to Default Position ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) ▶ Move Avatars & Garments to Default Position → Pop-up menu appears. 2. Click on 'Move Avatars & Garments to Default Position'. → Avatars and garments are now being moved to default position (0.0) in the 3D window.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for resetting avatars and garments to their default position in the 3D window.

title: Flip Horizontally/Vertically
content: ### Objective Flip Patterns/Internal Shapes horizontally or vertically as needed. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Flip Horizontally/ Flip Vertically (ver2.5.0) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Flip Horizontally/ Flip Vertically ### Operation 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Pattern Transform tool or the Edit Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Flip Horizontally/ Flip Vertically (ver2.5.0) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Flip Horizontally/ Flip Vertically →The selected Patterns/ Internal Shapes are flipped horizontally or vertically.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for flipping 2D patterns and internal shapes horizontally or vertically using the Pattern Transform tool or the Edit Pattern tool.

title: Copy/Paste Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Copy and paste multiple buttonholes with keeping the interval space evenly. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation #### Copy/Paste Buttonhole 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. 3. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. 4. Click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. #### Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Pase Buttonhole 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. 3. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. 4. Right click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. →The Paste window appears. 5. Input desired value for interval/number of buttonholes/position. Interval | Sets the distance between buttonholes. ---|--- Number of Buttons/Buttonholes | Sets the number of buttonholes to copy/paste. Position | Sets the position of the center of the copied button/buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline (ver2.5.0). 6. Click OK. → The buttonholes are now being created and applied accordingly.
content_description: This page provides step-by-step instructions for efficiently copying and pasting multiple buttonholes with evenly spaced intervals in your design.

title: ANIMATION MODE: Play Animation
content: ### Objective Play the recorded garment animation. ### Location Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor Upper Toolbar ※ Note #### Edit Animation Tools ![ani_btn_rec_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438440172313) (Record) | Records the motion of the avatar with the simulation of the garment ---|--- ![ani_btn_left_double_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438502052633) (Start) | Moves to the beginning of the play area. ![ani_btn_left_frame_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438502304537) (One Frame Back) | Steps one frame back ![ani_btn_play_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438440719257) (Start/Pause) | Plays the play area / Pauses temporarily on the play area. ![ani_btn_right_frame_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438502714905) (One Frame Forward) | Steps one frame forward ![ani_btn_right_double_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438502946713) (End) | Moves to the end of the play area. ![ani_btn_re_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438503133977) (Repeat) | Repeats the play area. ![ani_btn_1x_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438441426073) (1x) | Changes the play speed. (1/4x, 1/2x, 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x) ![icon_merge_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438503443993) (Merge) | Merge selected animation layers into a single layer. ![icon_cut_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438441721625) (Cut) | Split animation layer at current timeline position. ![icon_del_none.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438441881241) (Delete) | Deletes animation layer or Keyframe depending on selection. ![ani_btn_create](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438503901337) (Create Key) | Creates new keyframe at current timeline position. ![Simulation](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438442260889) (Simulation Quality / Type) | * Animation (Stable) * Normal (Default) * Custom ![Simulation](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438442260889) (Simulation Quality / Value) | The value is set on 1 by default. More value increases the detail of the recording. ![icon_setting_none_2.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438476093593) (Settings) | Animation settings pop-up menu * Frame Rate * Simulation Quality * Play Type * Playback Start/End * Scene Timewarp * Unit
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the features and tools available in the Animation Editor for playing and editing garment animations.

Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Trims Display Icon ▶ Show Bond/Skive → The selected area's bond/skive in the 3D window is now being shown or hidden.

title: Troubleshooting "MSVCP100.dll was not found" Error Message.
content: ### Objective Learn how to resolve launch error with missing MSVCP100.dll This is caused by missing or outdated Visual C++ Redistributable which essential Windows component to running Marvelous Designer software. ![error](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438429828505) ### ### **How to solve** * Visit [Microsoft website](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-US/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170), then download and install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable. The X64 architecture is recommended. ### **Note** * In some cases, you may need to remove older versions of the Visual C++ Redistributables installed on your computer. * The Visual C++ Redistributable is backward compatible with older versions, so we recommend installing only the most recent version.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to resolve the launch error caused by the missing MSVCP100.dll file by installing the latest Visual C++ Redistributable.

Navigate to 2D toolbar and select the Edit Pattern tool. 2. Select more than two points to be aligned. 3. Right click on the fiducial point and follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Points) ▶ Left / Center / Right / Top / Middle / Bottom / To Point (X-Axis) / To Point (Y-Axis) →The selected points are aligned according to the selected option.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for aligning multiple points along specified directions or axes using the Right Click Pop-Up Menu in the 2D toolbar.

Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing Tool ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Delete Sewing ※ Note: You can also select it and hit the Delete key on the keyboard to delete the Sewing Line.

title: Buttonhole Property Setting
content: ### Objective Adjust buttonhole properties such as Rotation Angle, Style and Bind Position. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation Selecting a buttonhole with Select/Move tool or Select/Move Button tool displays its properties in the Property Editor. Buttonhole Property | Description ---|--- Style | Select a buttonhole style. Angle | Enter desired value for Rotation Angle of buttonholes. Z-Offset (mm) | Adjust Z-Offset by entering a value. (Default Z-Offset: 0.13mm) Bind Position | Locate fastened buttons and buttonholes. ※ Note: From ver2.5.0, the location of the Bind Position has been moved from the Buttonhole Style Properties to an individual property. Therefore it is now available to edit individual buttons and buttonholes. 2D Measurement | View the position of buttonholes in 2D pattern with its size measurement. Set check-boxes On for Left/Right/Up/Down as desired. → The 2D size measurements appear accordingly.
content_description: This web page allows users to adjust and customize buttonhole properties, including rotation angle, style, and bind position, while providing a visual measurement of their placement in a 2D pattern.

title: Opacity Setting
content: ### Objective Adjust Opacity to express transparent or translucent materials. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Opacity ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Opacity 2. Move the Opacity scroll-bar to adjust. ※ Note: When the Opacity is at 0, the Garment no longer appears and becomes unable to select from the 3D window. It is recommended to set the rendering style to Show Thick Texture instead of Show Texture when checking invisible Garments.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on adjusting the opacity of materials in the Fabric Property Editor to achieve desired transparency effects in 3D garments.

title: Mirror Paste Button
content: ### Objective Copy and mirror paste buttons (ver2.5.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 2. Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. 3. Right click on the copied button then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. → Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click on a desired location to paste the buttons. ※ Note: * Before pasting buttons in place, right-click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttons can be manually input for multiple copy and paste. * When buttons are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide to using the Mirror Paste function for buttons in a 3D environment, allowing users to efficiently duplicate and position elements with mirrored placements.

title: Check Sewing Length

You can check unintended Sewing Line length difference made during the garment making process. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Check Sewing Length 2D Toolbar ▶ Check Sewing Length ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Check Sewing Length 2D Toolbar ▶ Check Sewing Length → The Sewing Lines with length difference greater than 5mm are bolded and highlighted in red.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to enable users to identify and assess significant differences in sewing line lengths during the garment making process, specifically highlighting discrepancies greater than 5mm for easy review.

Follow the indicated guideline below: Library ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric File (.zfab) → Preview of Fabric files is now being displayed below the Library section. ※ Note: Only fabric files saved in Marvelous Designer 4 and above are allowed to display Fabric information preview. For any fabric files created in previous versions, need to be saved again in ver3.1.0 or above (ver3.1.0).
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to preview fabric information in the Library window of Marvelous Designer, ensuring compatibility with the appropriate software versions.

title: 3D File (COLLADA) Import
content: ### Objective COLLADA is a commonly used 3D application format that can be exported from 3D tools such as 3DS Max, Maya, Poser, and DAZ Studio and used as Marvelous Designer Avatar or Scene/Prop. For 3DS Max or Maya, install the “OpenCOLLADA” plugin (<https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCOLLADA/wiki/OpenCOLLADA-Tools>) and use it to export in COLLADA format, instead of using the default COLLADA exporter. COLLADA files contain Geometry and Material, in addition to Rigging, Skinning, and Animation data. Avatar Motion Data can be imported into Marvelous Designer in COLLADA file format, then saved as a *.mtn file, which is Marvelous Designer's proprietary format. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OpenCOLLADA ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OpenCOLLADA → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → The Import COLLADA window opens. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. Object Type | Import as Avatar | Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame count into the Morphing Frame Count. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. ---|---|--- Import as Prop/Scene | The simulated object passes through the Garments due to a lack of collision. Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being imported when a value is entered Garment Position | Move Garment to Start Position | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: If the COLLADA file path includes # (symbols), the file may not load properly.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on exporting and importing COLLADA files for use in Marvelous Designer, including installation instructions for the OpenCOLLADA plugin and detailed operational steps for importing various object types.

title: ZIPPER: Slider Gizmo
content: ### Objective Move or rotate the slider to adjust its distance from the zipper tape. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation #### Move 1. Create a zipper. 2. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move 3. Click the slider. → The slider is selected and its Gizmo appears. 4. Click and drag the blue segment of the Gizmo to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. #### Rotate 1. With the Select/Move tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. 2. Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the Z axis. → The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. 3. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. → The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the Gizmo changes accordingly. 4. Rotate the puller referencing #2. ※ Note: To reset the slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select the Reset Slider Arrangement option.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for adjusting the position and rotation of a zipper slider within a 3D garment simulation.

title: Proxy Server Setting
content: * Note Marvelous Designer has removed the Proxy Server option from version 11 and onward, in order to enhance the security for users. If users however, wish to continue using the Proxy Server in their network system, then please refer below. **Objective** Set the proxy server through environment variables provided by the OS * Note: Only HTTP/HTTPS protocol is supported. **Operation** 1\. Click the start button on the taskbar. 2\. Click Edit environment variables. 3\. Environment Variables ▶System Variable ▶ Click the New... and enter the proxy server information **Information** | **When using IP** | **When Using User ID/ Password** ---|---|--- **Variable name** | PROXY_HTTP (Capital letter) * Note: When connecting to a proxy server using HTTPS, the variable name must be entered as PROXY_HTTPS. **Variable value** | ip:port E.g) 12.34.56.78:80 | Id:password@url:port E.g) MD:password123@example.com:8080 * Note: On Mac, you need to enter environment variables in Shell Profile. (Bash Shell: ~/.bash_profile, Z Shell: ~/.zprofile) ![__1.PNG](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438270782105) ![__2.PNG](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438257671577)
content_description: This web page provides instructions for setting up a proxy server using environment variables in Marvelous Designer versions 11 and onward, following the removal of the Proxy Server option for enhanced security.

title: Troubleshooting issues that may arise while running the program
content: The following issues may arise upon running the program 1. Sentinel HASP Driver failed to install properly ![Run_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438425400089) Though the Sentinel HASP Driver is installed alongside the program, there are cases where the Driver is not installed properly. This can be resolved by referring to the link below and manually installing the Sentinel HASP Driver. [Installing Sentinel HASP Driver Manually](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585) 2. Could not connect to the On-Line Authentication Server ![Run_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438425676953) Due to the user’s network setting or firewall, connections to the On-Line Authentication Server may fail. This can be resolved by following the link below and using the Off-Line License Key issued. [Troubleshooting On-Line Authentication Failure](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358427341465)
content_description: This webpage provides solutions for common issues encountered during program installation and authentication, including improper installation of the Sentinel HASP Driver and connection problems with the On-Line Authentication Server.

title: Add Color Swatch
content: ### Objective Add color swatches to custom palette. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color ▶ Color Palette Window ▶ Add ### Operation 1. Select a desired object; Avatar/Fabric/Button/Topstitch/Etc. 2. Click on Color in the Property Editor. → The Color Palette window appears. 3. Select a desired color from Open Palette or Palette Library. 4. Follow the indicated guideline below: Color Palette Window ▶ Add → The selected color is now being added to the custom palette.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding color swatches to your custom palette using the Color Palette window in the Property Editor.

title: Create Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Create buttonholes and place them as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole ### Operation #### Create Buttonhole 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. → A buttonhole is created. 3. Enter the number of garment layers and click OK. → The buttonholes are now being created. #### Input Measurement for Buttonhole Position 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Right-click on the 2D pattern where buttonholes would be placed. → The Moving Distance window appears. 3. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. → Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click OK to place. → The buttonholes are now being created.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating and accurately placing buttonholes on 3D garments and 2D patterns.

title: Tack
content: ### Objective Use this function to visualize fit adjustments by tacking temporarily. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack 2. Click on an initial point on a draped Garment. → A point is now being created with a dotted line following. 3. Click on an endpoint. → Another point is now being created with a yellow highlighted line. → Same tack is now being created in the 2D Pattern. 4. Activate Simulate. → The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to each other. ※ Note: It is also available to create and modify tacks in the 2D window (ver3.1.0). ###
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to using the Tack feature for visualizing fit adjustments on garments through temporary tacking.

title: Piping Property Setting
content: ### Objective Modify the physical Piping properties at Property Editor. ### Location Property Editor ### Explanation Piping properties appear in the Property Editor when a Piping is selected with the Select/Move tool or the Edit Piping tool. Information | Name | Renames selected Piping. ---|---|--- Line Length | Displays the line length of selected Piping. Dimension | Width (mm) | Adjusts the width of selected Piping between the value of 1~15mm. Particle Distance (mm) | Adjusts the Particle Distance of selected Piping between the value of 1~5mm. Finishing | Start | Close start of piping End | Close end of piping | Fabric | Applies fabric settings to selected Piping from the drop-down item list of Fabric. Piping's fabric texture can be edited using the edit_texture.png Edit Texture tool (ver4.2.0). Hide | Shows/hides selected Piping. (Select a Piping from the Scene tab in the Object Browser to reveal menu.)
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a comprehensive guide on modifying the physical properties of piping within the Property Editor, including renaming, adjusting dimensions, and applying fabric settings.

title: Play Motion
content: ### Objective Play Pose(*.pos) or Motion(*.mtn) files. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Play Motion 2D Toolbar ▶ Play Motion ### Operation #### Pose 1. Open a Pose file. → When a Pose file is loaded, the Play Motion tool is automatically activated. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Play Motion 2D Toolbar ▶ Play Motion 3. Click the Play Motion tool while the Avatar changes pose. → The Avatar stops temporarily. → The Avatar changes pose again. #### Motion 1. Open a Motion file. → The Play Motion tool now can be selected. 2. Click the Play Motion tool. → The motion is played. * The Transition Animation for the default avatars of the version 10 is not compatible with the previous versions.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for users on how to open and play Pose and Motion files for avatars using the Play Motion tool.

title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)
content: ### Objective Use the Property Editor to resize the texture applied to the Patterns. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ Property Editor ### Operation 1. Height | Set the texture height. Lock Aspect Ratio | Lock the width and height ratio.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the Property Editor to resize textures applied to Patterns within the Fabric tab of the Object Browser.

content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide to resetting Topstitch style properties to their default values in version 2.5.0.

title: 3D M:N Free Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing ※ Note: Hold down the Free Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Free Sewing Tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. ※ Note: * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users in utilizing the M:N Free Sewing tool to efficiently create and manage sewing lines across multiple patterns in both 2D and 3D environments.

title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Topstitch Face Setting
content: ### Objective Select the face of Topstitch. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Face ### Explanation ![topstitchFront.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438783711769) | Topstitch is only set for the front of the Fabric. ---|--- ![topstitchBack.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438783876377) | Topstitch is only set for the back of the Fabric. ![topstitchBoth.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438812482457) | Topstitch is set for the both sides of the Fabric. ※Note: Topstitch placed on the back of the Fabric do not appear in the 2D window (ver4.2.0).
